activity.notes: Burnaburiash I is identified in modern scholarship as the first Kassite dynast securely known to have ruled Babylonia, but the sixteenth- and early fifteenth-century BCE Kassite chronology is extremely poorly documented. ATLAS therefore does not fabricate a multi-year reign interval and instead places a representative c.1500 BCE reign point on the timeline.

sources.title: KASSITES — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Encyclopaedia Iranica states that the sixteenth- and fifteenth-century BCE emergence of the Kassite state is almost devoid of documentation and identifies Burnaburiash I as the first Kassite dynast who ruled Babylonia.

sources.title: Mesopotamian Chronology — Livius
sources.citation_text: The chronology survey emphasizes the limits of reconstructing early Kassite Babylonian reigns before the better-dated fourteenth century BCE.
